Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.14.3.
2. Create or load any world in any gamemode.
3. Place an anvil anywhere in the world.
4. Place an item on the anvil and rename it with any 18 character string.
5. Attempt to delete all text using Shift + Command + Delete.
6. Observe that the game crashes, displaying "saving world".
7. Note the crash report file generated in the `crash-reports` folder.
8. Take a screenshot of the crash message and the crash report file for documentation.
Observed Behavior: The game crashes when attempting to delete all text using Shift + Command + Delete on an anvil after renaming an item with any 18-character string in Minecraft version 1.14.3. To reproduce the issue, launch Minecraft and start or load any world from any gamemode. Place an item on the anvil and rename it with a string of exactly 18 characters. Attempting to delete all text using Shift + Command + Delete triggers the crash, which displays "saving world" before crashing. The crash report indicates a `java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range: -1` error during rendering screen operations. This issue occurs on both singleplayer and multiplayer modes and affects the anvil interface specifically when handling text deletion after renaming with 18 characters. Screenshots highlighting the crash, along with the debug folder contents and relevant log files, would provide further details for developers to diagnose and fix this bug.
Expected Behavior: When an item is placed on an anvil and renamed with any 18 character string, attempting to delete all text using shift command delete should successfully clear the name without crashing the game. The screen should update to show an empty input field, allowing further edits or exiting the anvil menu normally.
